entries.title: Psalms 32:1
segments: The probable occasion of this psalm was the season of anguish and remorse through which David passed in consequence of his sin in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

Covered; blotted out, pardoned. 
 
Forgiveness of sins is essential to happiness here or hereafter, and those who receive it may be pronounced truly blessed, both in this world and the world to come.

entries.title: Psalms 32:3
segments:
Kept silence; refused to confess his sins. 
 
  Waxed old; through the greatness of his distress.

entries.title: Psalms 32:4
segments: My moisture is turned into the drought of summer; he became emaciated and dried up nder the burden of his iniquities.

entries.title: Psalms 32:5
segments: Ingenuous confession of sin and hearty turning from it are essential to forgiveness; and those who will not confess and forsake it, must suffer its dreadful consequences for ever.

entries.title: Psalms 32:6
segments: For this; on account of God's readiness to pardon.

entries.title: Psalms 32:8
segments: Those who by repentance of sin and faith in Jesus Christ have turned to God and found pardoning mercy, are exceedingly anxious that others should take the same blessed way, and thus obtain rest, peace, and joy to their souls.

entries.title: Psalms 32:9
segments: The horse--the mule; which refuse to be governed except by force.

entries.title: Psalms 32:10
segments: The wicked; those who refuse to yield obedience to the divine will.
